checks.Title: Re-enter through change, not summary
checks.Evidence: The scene establishes present state through direct exposition of backstory rather than dramatized change: 'Twenty-one people walked onto a boat off Tidewell, eleven years ago, and fourteen came home... She'd promised herself, at a different window over this same lake, never to be sloppy again' and later Rook's monologue reciting the whole Axiom/Tidewell/Soraya history ('Not Axiom. Tidewell... Seven years before Soraya... The seven weren't the cost... They were the product') functions as summary delivered in dialogue, not as a changed present the reader reconstructs from.
checks.Fix: Cut the explicit Tidewell/Axiom recitations and instead let the changed present (Rook's rules, the crew's new dynamics, Soraya's four-year silence surfacing as behavior) carry the history implicitly, trusting small physical tells rather than spoken-aloud backstory to do the reminding.

checks.Title: Reintroduce names like an old friend would
checks.Evidence: Rook and Soraya get vivid in-voice reactivation tags (the three-finger count, chopstick precision), but crew members like Boiler, Scout, Lace, and Vox are reintroduced largely through Soraya's expository dossier ('He'll want the building before the job,' 'Scout's still in the Gray Zone... She's got Gerald') followed by a flashback anecdote each -- a structure closer to briefing-plus-backstory than a lived-in tag. Vox and Lace in particular are named and characterized entirely secondhand before they appear in person much later.
checks.Fix: Let each returning crew member's first on-page appearance carry its own single physical/behavioral beat the way Boiler's calibration wheel does, rather than front-loading their identity through Soraya's dialogue and a retrospective anecdote.

checks.Title: Refresh proprietary terms on a lighter touch than the gateway
Never an acronym before its term
checks.Evidence: Multiple acronyms appear with no in-voice expansion ever given: 'GLMZ' (used repeatedly, e.g. 'the vacuum rail that ran GLMZ's spine' and 'GLMZ doesn't stop being what it is'), 'NRST' ('the gray-market balance from the NRST crack'), and 'QUANTA' (used as a bare term throughout, e.g. 'no QUANTA mark' and 'a QUANTA figure that drops') never receive a full-term gloss before or after first use.
checks.Fix: Insert an in-voice expansion at each acronym's first appearance, e.g. have a character gloss 'GLMZ' as its full name once before using the bare initials, and similarly expand 'NRST' and 'QUANTA' the first time each appears on the page.

checks.Title: Pay the previous book its due, then move
checks.Evidence: The prose leans almost entirely on relitigating Tidewell (the previous book's ending) through extended flashback texture — Wennick's unspoken name, Boiler's collapsing floor, Lace's read, Vox's coffee ritual, the 'seven weren't the cost, they were the product' reveal — rather than briefly confirming that ending's weight and pivoting forward; the node spends thousands of words re-processing old guilt as active plot fuel instead of a compact acknowledging beat.
checks.Fix: Trim the Tidewell material to one clear, contained beat early on that confirms what it cost and that it stuck (e.g., the Wennick line and the count-promise alone), then let the new twenty-one crisis carry the forward momentum without repeatedly re-litigating the old wound as new revelations throughout the piece.

checks.Title: Open the door the last ending left ajar
checks.Evidence: The prose repeatedly names the inherited Tidewell thread ('Fourteen out of twenty-one, off Tidewell,' 'a name at the bottom of it you don't say out loud') and complicates it well by mapping it onto the new twenty-one and Rook's confession that 'The seven weren't the cost. They were the product' -- but this recontextualization depends entirely on backstory (Tidewell, Wennick, Axiom) that a first-time reader has no anchor for, so the 'door left ajar' is being opened almost exclusively for returning readers rather than being legible as a planted question from a specific prior ending.
checks.Fix: Add one grounding beat early that frames Tidewell explicitly as 'the job the last book ended on' with enough concrete stakes (what readers saw resolved, what was left unresolved) that a newcomer can feel the echo as continuity rather than untethered lore.

checks.Title: Reward the long memory without taxing the short one
checks.Evidence: The current plot's legibility depends on absorbing dense unexplained backstory delivered as fact rather than reintroduced context: 'Twenty-one people walked onto a boat off Tidewell, eleven years ago, and fourteen came home' is dropped in without scene-setting, and later the Axiom job, the routing code Rook 'read... four years ago, burned into the side of a tank while the tank was trying to kill her,' Vox's 'retail-grade, sold the second tier in the Gray Zone' history, and Goldberg's four-year-old defection are all treated as load-bearing knowledge the reader must already hold to track who owes whom what and why the vault-crack plan works.
checks.Fix: Add brief in-scene grounding for each callback the first time it's invoked (a line of context for Tidewell, Axiom, and Vox's proxy-network backstory) so a first-time reader can follow the present mission's stakes and character motivations without already knowing the prior book's events.

checks.Title: Escalate, don't repeat
checks.Evidence: The structural spine repeats Tidewell almost beat for beat (twenty-one names, a survivor count, a betrayal by a trusted ally who withheld the truth, a crew assembled by trait-based vignettes, a final tally written on paper) — even the closing beach/lake beat and 'that's not the same thing' reckoning mirror what the text says already happened once before, so the sequel's engine is explicitly the same engine re-run with new labels (Marrow instead of Axiom, Anneke instead of an unnamed handler).
checks.Fix: Cut or radically compress the Tidewell-parallel scaffolding (the recruiting montage, the exact 21-count echo) and let the new wrinkle — three facilities still running, Rook choosing not to chase them yet — become the actual spine of the story instead of a coda tacked onto a rerun, so the piece escalates into unresolved moral scale rather than resolving into another clean count.
